# Safe code review: `a9c863e…HEAD`

**Mode:** read-only draft. I ran the nine review areas myself instead of spawning the per-area agents and the validator/refuter pairs. None of the findings were adjudicated (0 of 8), so there is **no score and no verdict**. Treat this as a `--quick`-style draft.

**Scope:** the merge-base of `a9c863e` and HEAD is `37e1073` (HEAD~1), so the three-dot diff is one commit, `eb4efcc` ("feat(safenet): surface the check as an audit-log step with attestation link"). That's 17 files, +680 −11. Nothing was uncommitted inside that scope.

**Repo:** Safe{Wallet} monorepo, TypeScript/React. Jest runs the tests; ESLint, Prettier and tsc are the gates. The written rules come from the root `AGENTS.md` and `apps/web/AGENTS.md`. The change doesn't touch onchain code.

## Summary

| | |
|---|---|
| Must-fix before opening | None found |
| Worth fixing or ticketing | 4 small correctness or cost issues, all P3 |
| Conventions | 2 gaps: a missing Storybook story and an undocumented env var |
| Security | Nothing found. The link `href` is built from hex hashes in chain logs or a fixed explorer base, and the oracle allowlist is unchanged. |
| Regression | Nothing found. The new `AuditRow` props are optional. `attestedAtMs` is a required field, but it's built at the only two construction sites, and mobile doesn't persist this cache. |

## Findings

| # | Area | Where | Finding |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Bugs | `apps/web/src/components/transactions/TxSigners/index.tsx:173` | `showsSafenetRow` repeats the row's render check but doesn't check that the feature has loaded. If the Safenet data arrives before the lazy feature chunk, `showsSafenetRow` is true while `<safenet.SafenetAuditRow>` (line 299) still renders the null stub. The last signing row then drops `isLast` and the timeline connector hangs with nothing under it until the chunk loads. **Fix:** also check that the feature is loaded (`!safenet.$isReady` / `$isDisabled`). Better, have the feature return a "will render" flag so the two checks can't drift apart; the code comment already warns that they can. |
| 2 | Performance | `packages/store/src/safenet/safenetCheckApi.ts:53-60` | The comment says the header read costs "one RPC per settled check" because polling stops. That's false while a check is in `AWAITING_VERIFICATION`: if `verifyAttestation` can't read the group key, it returns `PENDING` and polling keeps going every 6s. Every one of those polls also calls `blockTimeMs`. The cost is capped by the deadline window, but it adds one RPC per poll. **Fix:** skip the header read unless the attestation is `VERIFIED`, or reuse the previous `attestedAtMs`. At minimum, correct the comment. |
| 3 | Bugs / UX | `apps/web/src/features/safenet-checks/components/SafenetAuditRow.tsx:104` | `timestamp={snapshot.attestedAtMs}` is only set when an attestation event exists. So "Risk detected" (`MALICIOUS`, which comes from a negative-verdict event) and "Safenet check failed" (`TIMED_OUT`) never show a date. The most important step is the one that's undated. The comment ("Null while running or when the header read failed") doesn't mention either case. **Fix:** date the step from the event that decided the status (the verdict event's block), or at least make the comment accurate. |
| 4 | DRY | `SafenetAuditRow.tsx:78-80` and `safenetCheckApi.ts:50-52` | "Prefer the oracle attestation, fall back to the plain one" is written out twice. If the store's choice changes, the link can point at a different transaction than the one that was verified. **Fix:** export one `selectAttestedEvent(events)` helper from `@safe-global/utils/features/safenet-checks` and use it in both places. |
| 5 | Conventions | `apps/web/src/features/safenet-checks/components/SafenetAuditRow.tsx:1` | The new component has no Storybook story. `apps/web/AGENTS.md:10` ("When making a new component, create a Storybook story file for it") and `:148` (component with logic → test + story) both require one. The five status states plus dark mode are exactly what a story should cover. |
| 6 | Conventions | `packages/utils/src/features/safenet-checks/constants.ts:53-55` | This commit adds `NEXT_PUBLIC_SAFENET_EXPLORER_URL` / `EXPO_PUBLIC_SAFENET_EXPLORER_URL`, but `apps/web/.env.example` doesn't list it. The same commit documents every other `SAFENET_*` variable there. |
| 7 | Testing | `apps/web/src/features/safenet-checks/components/__tests__/SafenetAuditRow.test.tsx` | Nothing tests the `TIMED_OUT` → "Safenet check failed" label (the test file never mentions `TIMED_OUT`). Nothing tests the dark-mode icon colours (`DARK_STEP_COLOR`) either. `MALICIOUS`, `BENIGN` and in-flight states are covered. |
| 8 | KISS | `SafenetAuditRow.tsx:79-80` | `snapshot?.events` uses optional chaining after line 68 has already returned when `!snapshot`. It's harmless but suggests `snapshot` could be undefined at that point. |

## Worth tidying (no score impact)
- #8 above: drop the redundant `?.`. That's 2 lines.
- The diff has far more comments than the code around it, and the root `AGENTS.md` says to "treat code comments as tech debt". The long block comments in `TxSigners/index.tsx:166-172`, `:296-298` and `safenetCheckApi.ts:53-55` could be much shorter, especially once #1 and #2 are fixed.

## Ruled out
- **Bundle cost from `TxSigners` importing `useSafenetCheck` directly, outside the lazy feature:** `safenetCheckApi` is already imported into `apps/web/src/store/index.ts:32`, so the direct import adds nothing to the main bundle.
- **Double chain reads:** the `TxSigners` subscription and the row's own subscription share one cache entry (`serializeQueryArgs` keys by hash), and both pass the same `submittedAt`.
- **`blockTimeMs` failure suppressing a verdict:** it catches its own errors and returns `null`, so `Promise.all` can't reject because of it. The new tests cover this.
- **Feature flag off:** the hash is `undefined`, so the query is skipped, and there's a test for that.

## Not checked
- I didn't run type-check, lint or tests, as asked.
- The per-area agents and the paired validation step weren't run, so every finding above is unconfirmed.
- I didn't check the rendered UI or the dark-mode colours visually.

Some claude.ai connectors (Slack, Google Drive, Datadog and others) need authorizing in your claude.ai connector settings before they can be used. This review didn't need any of them.
